titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Adrami's Judgment, Edom, and Karmin (ch. 73–75)
part: ch. 73–75 — Adrami's Judgment, Edom, and Karmin
about: Chapter 73 gives Adrami's first judgment in the sheep-and-vineyard case; Baltasar, amazed, names him his heir, and Adrami becomes king of Rome, the world's kingship having been given to Shem's seed. Chapter 74 turns to the king of Midian and traces the line of Esau and Edom, using Esau's lost birthright to preach that the soul must bind the flesh, with sayings of Paul and of Christ to his disciples. Chapter 75 begins the story of Karmin, a rich and pious man of Judah who settles in Armathaim and draws Satan's envy.

sentences.t: ፸፫ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ቀዳሜ ፡ ፍትሑ ፡ ለአድራሚ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ሮም ።
sentences.l: 73. Concerning first-of his-judgment to-Adrami king-of Rome.
sentences.i: Chapter 73: Concerning the first judgment of Adrami, king of Rome.
sentences.n: Chapter heading. በእንተ ‘concerning’ + ቀዳሜ, construct of ቀዳሚ ‘first, beginning’, + ፍትሑ ‘his judgment’ (ፍትሕ + -ሁ); the text then follows with ለአድራሚ ‘to Adrami’, a ለ- of possession that doubles the suffix (‘his judgment, Adrami's’), then ንጉሠ ሮም ‘king-of Rome’. The number ፸፫ is 73, spoken ሰብዓ ወሠለስቱ (säbʿa wä-śälästu). The previous part broke off before the verdict in the sheep-and-vineyard case; the new chapter opens with it.

sentences.t: ወይቤሎሙ ፡ ስምዑኒ ፡ ዘእፈትሕ ፡ ለክሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-said-to-them: hear-me what I-judge for-you;
sentences.i: And he said to them: Listen to me, to what I judge for you.
sentences.n: ወይቤሎሙ ‘and he said to them’ (ይቤ, the defective verb ‘say’, + ሎሙ ‘to them’ with ወ-). Adrami speaks, since Baltasar answers him in unit 5. ስምዑኒ is the imperative ሰምዑ ‘hear (pl.)’ + -ኒ ‘me’. ዘእፈትሕ ‘that which I judge’ (ዘ + imperfect 1cs of ፈትሐ ‘judge’), ለክሙ ‘for you (pl.)’.

sentences.t: ለእመ ፡ ሠረዋ ፡ አሕሩገ ፡ ጒንዲ ፡ ሥረዎን ፡ ወኵሎን ፡ ለከ ፡ ወለእመ ፡ በልዓ ፡ ቈጽለ ፡ አዕጹቅ ፡ ወጽጌ ፡ ቆዕ ፡ ንሣእ ፡ ቅርፅ ፡ ፀምሮን ፡ ወደቂቆን ፡ እለ ፡ ኢተበኵራ ፤
sentences.l: If they-uprooted shoots-of stock their-roots and-all-of-them, to-you; and-if they-(f.)-ate foliage-of shoots and-blossom-of tendril, take fleece-of their-wool and-their-young, those which not-bore-firstborn;
sentences.i: If the sheep uprooted the shoots of the vine-stock, roots and all, they are yours; and if they ate the foliage of the shoots and the blossom of the tendril, take the fleece of their wool and their young, those that have not yet borne a first-born (?);
sentences.n: ለእመ ‘if’ with the perfect ሠረዋ (ሠረወ ‘root out, uproot’, 3fp, the sheep as feminine plural); አሕሩገ ጒንዲ is a construct, ‘shoots (?) of the stock/trunk (?)’, and ሥረዎን ወኵሎን ‘their roots and all of them’ (-ን 3fp), ለከ ‘to you’, i.e. the animals become the vineyard owner's. The second ‘if’ has በልዓ ‘they (f.) ate’ (3fp, the same ending as ሠረዋ, so the same subject, the sheep; a 3ms ‘he ate’ would be በልዐ): ቈጽለ ‘foliage, leaves’, አዕጹቅ (?) a plural I take as ‘shoots’, ወጽጌ ቆዕ ‘and blossom of the tendril’ (?). This echoes the owner's plea in the previous part (‘it ate it only when the tendril had put forth blossom’). ንሣእ is the imperative of ነሥአ ‘take’; ቅርፅ ‘rind, outer covering’ is my best guess for the fleece (?). እለ ኢተበኵራ ‘those (f.) which have not borne a firstborn’ (ተበኵረ) is also uncertain (?). The verdict is a split by status of the ewes.

sentences.t: ወእለሰ ፡ ተበኵራ ፡ ወወለዳ ፡ ኅድግ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ለባዕለ ፡ አባግዕ ።
sentences.l: And-those-but which-bore-firstborn and-gave-birth, leave to-him, to-owner-of sheep.
sentences.i: But those that have borne a first-born and given birth, leave to him, to the owner of the sheep.
sentences.n: ወእለሰ ‘but as for those who’ (-ሰ contrast); ተበኵራ ወወለዳ ‘they (f.) bore a firstborn and gave birth’. ኅድግ is the imperative of ኀደገ ‘leave’, ሎቱ ‘to him’; ለባዕለ አባግዕ ‘to the owner-of sheep’ (ባዕል ‘owner, lord’ in the construct, አባግዕ plural of በግዕ ‘sheep’). Ewes that have already borne remain with their owner.

sentences.t: ወአንከርዎ ፡ ኵሎሙ ፡ እለ ፡ ሰምዑ ፡ አውሥኦተ ፡ ፍትሑ ።
sentences.l: And-they-marvelled-at-him, all those-who heard the-answer-of his-judgment.
sentences.i: And all who heard the answer of his judgment marvelled at him.
sentences.n: አንከርዎ is the perfect 3mp of አንከረ ‘marvel, be astonished’ + -ዎ ‘him’ (the ወ- is ‘and’). ኵሎሙ ‘all of them’ is the subject, then the relative እለ ሰምዑ ‘who heard’. አውሥኦተ ‘answer, response’ is the accusative of አውሥኦት (from አውሥአ ‘answer’), with ፍትሑ ‘his judgment’ in construct.

sentences.t: ወይቤ ፡ በልጣሶር ፡ በአማን ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ ፍትሕ ፡ ፍትሐ ፡ ሕዝበ ፡ አምላከ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ወእምይእዜሰ ፡ ለዘሂ ፡ ይትዋቀሥ ፡ ፍታሕ ፡ ወለዘሂ ፡ ይፀብእ ፡ ፅባእ ፡ ወለዘሂ ፡ ይትኴነን ፡ ኰንን ፡ ወለዘሂ ፡ የሐዩ ፡ አሕዩ ፡ ወለኵሉ ፡ በከመ ፡ ፍትሑ ፡ ፍታሕ ፡ ወንሥኣ ፡ ለዛቲ ፡ ሀገር ፡ ለከ ፡ ወለዘርእከ ፡ እምድኅሬከ ።
sentences.l: And-said Baltasar: in-truth this judgment is-judgment-of people-of God-of Israel; and-from-now-but for-whoever-also he-contends, judge; and-for-whoever-also he-fights, fight; and-for-whoever-also he-is-judged, condemn; and-for-whoever-also he-lives, give-life; and-for-all according-to his-judgment, judge; and-take this city for-you and-for-your-seed after-you.
sentences.i: And Baltasar said: In truth, this judgment is the judgment of the people of the God of Israel. From now on, for whoever contends, give judgment; for whoever goes to war, make war; for whoever is to be judged, pass sentence; for whoever is to live, grant life; and for everyone, judge according to his judgment (?). And take this city for yourself and for your seed after you.
sentences.n: Baltasar's response, built on a run of imperatives. በአማን ‘in truth’; ፍትሐ ሕዝበ አምላከ እስራኤል is a three-link chain, ‘judgment-of people-of God-of Israel’: he credits the verdict to the God of Israel, not to Adrami's wit. ወእምይእዜሰ ‘and from now on’. Each clause pairs ለዘሂ ‘for whoever’ with an imperfect and then an imperative of the same root: ይትዋቀሥ (ተዋቀሠ ‘dispute, contend’) ፍታሕ ‘judge’; ይፀብእ (ፀብአ ‘make war’) ፅባእ ‘fight’; ይትኴነን (ተኰነነ ‘be judged, condemned’) ኰንን ‘condemn’; የሐዩ ‘lives’ አሕዩ ‘give life’ (the causative of ሐይወ), a royal power of life and death. በከመ ፍትሑ ‘according to his judgment/right’ (?) could also mean ‘as he is judged’. ወንሥኣ is ንሣእ ‘take’ + -ኣ ‘her’ (3fs), ‘take it (the city)’. ለዘርእከ ‘for your seed’ and እምድኅሬከ ‘after you’. So Baltasar makes Adrami his heir. ሕዝብ ‘people’ is the Old Testament phrase for Israel; the whole speech reads as Adrami's kingship ratified.

sentences.t: ወሠምሩ ፡ ኵሎሙ ፡ ሰብአ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ሮሜ ፡ ወአንገሥዎ ፡ ላዕሌሆሙ ፡ ወተፈሥሑ ፡ ቦቱ ፡ ዐቢየ ፡ ፍሥሓ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-were-pleased all-of-them men-of city-of Rome and-they-made-him-king over-them and-they-rejoiced in-him a-great joy;
sentences.i: And all the people of the city of Rome were pleased, and made him king over them, and rejoiced in him with great joy;
sentences.n: ሠምሩ ‘they were pleased’ (perfect 3mp of ሠምረ), ሰብአ ሀገረ ሮሜ ‘men-of city-of Rome’ (note ሮሜ here and ሮም in the heading, two spellings). አንገሥዎ ‘they made him king’ (the causative አንገሠ + him) ላዕሌሆሙ ‘over them’. ተፈሥሑ ቦቱ ‘they rejoiced in him’; ዐቢየ ፍሥሓ ‘great joy’ is a cognate accusative (the verb and ፍሥሓ share the root ፈሠሐ).

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ በፈቃዶሙ ፡ ወበፈቃደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ኮነ ፡ ከመዝ ።
sentences.l: for by-their-will and-by-will-of God it-was thus.
sentences.i: for it was by their will and by the will of God that it was so.
sentences.n: እስመ ‘for’ gives the reason. በፈቃዶሙ ‘by their will’ (ፈቃድ + -ሙ) and በፈቃደ እግዚኣብሔር ‘by the will-of God’, a construct. ኮነ ከመዝ ‘it was thus’. The pairing of the people's will with God's is the book's theme that kings are chosen by God and received by the people.

sentences.t: ወአኀዞ ፡ ፈፀንት ፡ ለበልጣሶር ፡ ወእምአሜሃ ፡ ይልእኮ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ፀብእ ፡ ወውስተ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ዘፈቀደ ፡ ወውእቱሰ ፡ ይነብር ፡ ሀገረ ።
sentences.l: And-seized-him ፈፀንት(?), Baltasar, and-from-then he-would-send-him to battle and-into all what he-wished; and-he-but would-stay in-the-city.
sentences.i: And ፈፀንት (?) took hold of Baltasar, and from then on he would send him to battle and into anything he wished, while he himself stayed in the city.
sentences.n: አኀዞ is አኀዘ ‘seize, hold’ + -ኦ ‘him’, restated by ለበልጣሶር ‘Baltasar’: the ለ- that marks the object and doubles the suffix (as with ለባዕለ in unit 3), so Baltasar is the one seized. ፈፀንት ends in -ት like a feminine noun and is then the subject. It is a word I cannot place (?); an affliction or infirmity would suit the sequel (Baltasar sends Adrami out, then dies in unit 9), but that is a guess from the sense (?). ወእምአሜሃ ‘and from then’. ይልእኮ ‘he sends him’ (imperfect of ለአከ + ‘him’), used habitually (‘would send’). ኀበ ፀብእ ‘to battle’, ውስተ ኵሉ ዘፈቀደ ‘into all that he wished’. ወውእቱሰ ‘and he, for his part’ marks the change of subject; ይነብር ሀገረ ‘he stays (in) the city’ with ሀገረ in the accusative of place.

sentences.t: ወእምድኅረዝ ፡ ሞተ ፡ በልጣሶር ፡ ወአርትዐ ፡ መንግሥተ ፤
sentences.l: And-after-this died Baltasar and-he-set-right the-kingdom;
sentences.i: And after this Baltasar died, and he set the kingdom in order (?);
sentences.n: ወእምድኅረዝ ‘and after this’ (እምድኅረ + ዝ). ሞተ ‘died’. አርትዐ is the causative of ርትዐ ‘be straight, right’: ‘made straight, set in order’ (?). The subject is not marked: it may be Baltasar (setting the kingdom in order before he died) or, perhaps more naturally after ሞተ, Adrami (?); the verb could also carry a different sense, ‘the kingdom was rightly ordered’.

sentences.t: ወኮነት ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ሮሜ ፡ ለአድራሚ ፡ ለትውልደ ፡ ትውልዲ ፡ እስመ ፡ በፈቃደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ተውህበ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ መንግሥተ ፡ ዓለም ፡ ለዘርአ ፡ ሴም ፡ ወግብርናት ፡ ለዘርአ ፡ ካም ፡ ወጒዕትያ ፡ ለዘርአ ፡ ያፌት ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-became(f) city-of Rome to-Adrami for-generation-of generation, for by-will-of God was-given all kingdom-of world to-seed-of Shem and-servitude to-seed-of Ham and-ጒዕትያ(?) to-seed-of Japheth.
sentences.i: And the city of Rome became Adrami's for all generations, since by the will of God the whole kingdom of the world was given to the seed of Shem, servitude to the seed of Ham, and ጒዕትያ (?) to the seed of Japheth.
sentences.n: ኮነት ‘it became’ (f.) agrees with ሀገረ. ለአድራሚ ‘to Adrami’, ለትውልደ ትውልዲ ‘for the generation of generation’, i.e. for all generations (ትውልዲ for ትውልድ is Bezold's spelling (?)). The reason (እስመ): the sons of Noah (Genesis 9–10) receive different lots, with Shem as bearer of kingship (a claim of the book). ተውህበ ‘was given’, passive of ወሀበ; መንግሥተ ዓለም ‘kingdom-of world’. ግብርናት is the abstract of ገብር ‘servant’: servitude, echoing Noah's curse on Ham's line (Genesis 9:25). ጒዕትያ is a word I cannot place (?); set against ‘kingship’ and ‘servitude’ it stands for some third portion. The row of ፨ marks the end of the chapter; the previous part ended the same way.

sentences.t: ፸፬ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ምድያም ።
sentences.l: 74. Concerning king-of Midian.
sentences.i: Chapter 74: Concerning the king of Midian.
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ንጉሠ is the construct of ንጉሥ; ምድያም is Midian (a son of Abraham and Keturah in Genesis 25:2; the chapter itself goes on to speak of Esau and Edom). The number ፸፬ is 74, spoken ሰብዓ ወአርባዕቱ (säbʿa wä-ʾärbaʿtu).

sentences.t: ንጉሠ ፡ ምድያምሂ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ሤም ፡ ውእቱ ፤
sentences.l: King-of Midian-also, seed-of Shem(ሤም) is-he;
sentences.i: The king of Midian too is of the seed of Shem;
sentences.n: ንጉሠ ምድያምሂ ‘king-of Midian-also’ (-ሂ ‘also, indeed’). ዘርአ ሤም ‘seed-of Shem’, with Shem written ሤም here but ሴም elsewhere in this part: one name, two spellings. ውእቱ is the ‘he is’ that closes the statement.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ይስሐቅ ፡ ዔሳው ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ዘወፅአ ፡ እምከርሠ ፡ እሙ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይእኅዞ ፡ ያዕቆብ ፡ በሰኰናሁ ፡ ወሄደ ፡ ብኵርናቱ ፡ ለዔሳው ፡ በእንተ ፡ ተብሲለ ፡ ብርስን ፡ ወበስመ ፡ ጽዕለቱ ፡ ተሰምየ ፡ ስመ ፡ መንግሥቱ ፡ እስመ ፡ ኤዶም ፡ ትርጒምናሁ ፡ ብርስን ፡ ብሂል ፤
sentences.l: for the-seed-of Isaac is Esau, he-who came-out from-womb-of his-mother while Jacob held-him by-his-heel, and-went(?) his-birthright, Esau's, because-of the-cooking-of lentils; and-by-name-of his-redness(?) he-was-named the-name-of his-kingdom, for Edom, its-interpretation lentils, saying;
sentences.i: for the seed of Isaac is Esau, who came out of his mother's womb while Jacob held him by the heel, and Esau's birthright was lost (?) on account of a cooking of lentils; and by the name of his redness (?) he was named, the name of his kingdom, for Edom, its interpretation, is ‘lentils’, that is to say;
sentences.n: The story is Genesis 25:24–34: the twins, Jacob holding Esau's heel (ሰኰና, ‘heel’ here, normally ‘hoof’), and the birthright sold for lentil stew. ዘወፅአ ‘who came out’; እምከርሠ እሙ ‘from the womb of his mother’ (ከርሥ ‘belly, womb’); እንዘ ይእኅዞ ‘while he was holding him’. ሄደ ብኵርናቱ ለዔሳው ‘his birthright went, Esau’s’: ሄደ looks like the Amharic-type form of ‘went’ (beside ሖረ), with the birthright as subject and ለዔሳው marking possession, so ‘was lost’ by idiom (?). በእንተ ተብሲለ ብርስን ‘on account of the cooking of lentils’ (ተብሲል, a verbal noun, ‘being cooked’ (?)). ጽዕለቱ ‘his redness’ (?): the Bible links Edom (Hebrew ʾĔdom) with ‘red’, but this text glosses the name as ‘lentils’; ኤዶም ትርጒምናሁ ብርስን ብሂል ‘Edom, its interpretation, lentils, saying’ is an explanatory aside, ‘that is to say’. ትርጒምናሁ ‘its interpretation’ is an unusual suffixed form. This is the book's own etymology; Genesis 25:30 ties the name Edom to the red stew of the same episode.

sentences.t: ወበእንተዝኬ ፡ ተሰምዩ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ዔሳው ፡ ኤዶማውያነ ፡ እስመ ፡ በስጥመተ ፡ ከርሡ ፡ ኀደገ ፡ ወተስዕረ ፡ እምብኵርናተ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ሴም ፡ እስመ ፡ ለእመ ፡ ኢተአስረት ፡ ነፍስ ፡ በትዕግሥት ፡ ያወርዶ ፡ ለኵሉ ፡ ዘሥጋ ፡ ፍትወተ ፡ ከርሥ ፡ ውስተ ፡ መሥገርት ፤
sentences.l: and-therefore were-named the-seed-of Esau Edomites, for through-the-plunging(?) of-his-belly he-left and-was-cast-out from-birthright-of seed-of Shem; for if not is-bound the-soul by-patience, brings-him-down every-one of-flesh the-desire-of belly into snare;
sentences.i: and for this reason the seed of Esau were called Edomites, because through the plunging of his belly (?) he left, and was cast out of, the birthright of the seed of Shem; for if the soul is not bound by patience, the desire of the belly brings every fleshly person down into a snare (?);
sentences.n: ወበእንተዝኬ ‘and for this reason’ (-ኬ ‘so, then’); ተሰምዩ ‘they were named’, ኤዶማውያነ ‘Edomites’ (accusative plural). በስጥመተ ከርሡ ‘through the plunging/absorption of his belly’ (?), i.e. gluttony. ኀደገ ‘he left, gave up’, ተስዕረ ‘he was defeated, deprived’ (?) with እምብኵርናተ ‘from the birthright’. The moral reading follows Hebrews 12:16, which calls Esau profane for one meal. ለእመ ኢተአስረት ነፍስ ‘if the soul is not bound’ (3fs, ነፍስ feminine), በትዕግሥት ‘by patience, endurance’; ያወርዶ ‘brings him down’ (አውረደ) ለኵሉ ዘሥጋ ‘every one of flesh’, with ፍትወተ ከርሥ ‘the desire-of belly’ taken as subject (?), though it stands in the accusative form; ውስተ መሥገርት ‘into a snare, trap’ (compare Psalm 91:3).

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ሥጋሰ ፡ ሥሥዕት ፡ ወነፍስሰ ፡ እስርት ፡ በትዕግሥት ፤
sentences.l: for flesh-but is-loosed(?) and-soul-but bound by-patience;
sentences.i: for the flesh is loose (?), but the soul is bound by patience;
sentences.n: ሥጋሰ … ወነፍስሰ ‘flesh, for its part … and soul, for its part’: the two -ሰ give an antithesis. ሥሥዕት (?) is a word I cannot parse with confidence; as the counterpart of እስርት ‘bound’ (a feminine noun or participle of አሰረ ‘bind’ (?)), I take it as ‘loosened, unrestrained’. በትዕግሥት ‘by patience’.

sentences.t: ወበእንተዝ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ጳውሎስ ፡ ዘኢትፈቱ ፡ ነፍስ ፡ ትፈቱ ፡ ሥጋ ፡ ወዘኢትፈቱ ፡ ሥጋ ፡ ትፈቱ ፡ ነፍስ ፡ ወክልኤሆን ፡ ይትኣበያ ፡ በበይናቲሆን ።
sentences.l: And-therefore said Paul: what the-soul does-not-desire, the-flesh desires; and-what the-flesh does-not-desire, the-soul desires; and-the-two-of-them oppose-each-other among-themselves.
sentences.i: And therefore Paul said: What the soul does not desire, the flesh desires; and what the flesh does not desire, the soul desires; and the two of them resist each other.
sentences.n: The saying is a paraphrase of Galatians 5:17 (the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; they are opposed to each other), cast as ‘soul’ against ‘flesh’ in place of ‘Spirit’. ጳውሎስ is Paul. ዘኢትፈቱ ነፍስ ‘what the soul does not desire’ (ፈተወ imperfect 3fs, ኢ- negative), ትፈቱ ሥጋ ‘the flesh desires’ (ሥጋ taken as feminine here). ወክልኤሆን ‘and the two of them’ (feminine plural -ሆን, agreeing with ነፍስ and ሥጋ); ይትኣበያ ‘they (f.) resist/oppose each other’ (reciprocal ተኣበየ, 3fp); በበይናቲሆን ‘between themselves’.

sentences.t: ለእመ ፡ አጥብዐ ፡ ብእሲ ፡ ወኀብረት ፡ ነፍሱ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ፍትወተ ፡ ሥጋሁ ፡ ይከውን ፡ ከመ ፡ ዲያብሎስ ፤
sentences.l: If he-strengthened(?) a-man and-joined his-soul with desire-of his-flesh, he-becomes like the-devil;
sentences.i: If a man gives strength to the flesh (?), and his soul joins with the desire of his flesh, he becomes like the devil;
sentences.n: ለእመ ‘if’ with the perfect አጥብዐ. I take it as ‘made strong/gave free rein’ and the object the flesh, understood (?); the meaning is clear from the opposite clause that follows (‘binds his flesh’). ኀብረት ነፍሱ ምስለ ፍትወተ ሥጋሁ ‘his soul joined with the desire of his flesh’ (ኀብረ ‘join’, perfect 3fs). ይከውን ከመ ዲያብሎስ ‘he becomes like the devil’ (imperfect of ኮነ + ከመ ‘like’).

sentences.t: ወለእመሰ ፡ አሰረ ፡ ሥጋሁ ፡ ወኀብረ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ፍትወተ ፡ ነፍሱ ፡ ይከውን ፡ ከመ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፤
sentences.l: and-if-but he-bound his-flesh and-joined with desire-of his-soul, he-becomes like Christ;
sentences.i: but if he binds his flesh and joins himself to the desire of his soul, he becomes like Christ;
sentences.n: The mirror of the previous unit: ወለእመሰ ‘but if’; አሰረ ሥጋሁ ‘he bound his flesh’; ኀብረ ‘he joined’ (3ms, without an expressed object; ‘himself’ is understood). ይከውን ከመ ክርስቶስ ‘he becomes like Christ’. The two outcomes, devil and Christ, lead into the next unit, where Christ is named as the head.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ብእሲ ፡ ዘየሐውር ፡ በፍኖት ፡ ርትዕት ፡ ርእሱ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ይቤሉ ፡ ሐዋርያት ።
sentences.l: for every man who-walks in-way righteous, his-head Christ, said the-apostles.
sentences.i: for every man who walks in a righteous way has Christ as his head, the apostles said.
sentences.n: ኵሉ ብእሲ ዘየሐውር ‘every man who walks’ (ዘ + imperfect of ሖረ); በፍኖት ርትዕት ‘in a way (that is) straight/righteous’ (ፍኖት feminine, agreeing with ርትዕት). ርእሱ ክርስቶስ ‘his head (is) Christ’, a nominal clause; compare 1 Corinthians 11:3 and Ephesians 5:23. ይቤሉ ሐዋርያት ‘the apostles said’, a closing formula that names the apostles as the source, as the author names Paul in unit 16.

sentences.t: ወእግዚእነሂ ፡ ይቤሎሙ ፡ ለአርዳኢሁ ፡ በመንፈስ ፡ ሖሩ ፡ ወፍትወተ ፡ ሥጋክሙ ፡ ኢትግበሩ ፤
sentences.l: And-our-Lord-also said-to-them to-his-disciples: in-spirit go, and-desire-of your-flesh do-not-do;
sentences.i: And our Lord also said to his disciples: Go in the spirit, and do not do the desire of your flesh;
sentences.n: እግዚእነ ‘our Lord’ (እግዚእ + -ነ) with -ሂ ‘also’. ይቤሎሙ ለአርዳኢሁ ‘he said to them, to his disciples’ (አርዳኢ is the plural of ረድእ ‘disciple’). ሖሩ is the imperative of ሖረ ‘go, walk’, በመንፈስ ‘in the spirit’; the instruction is Galatians 5:16 (‘walk in the Spirit and you will not fulfil the desire of the flesh’), put in Jesus' mouth. ኢትግበሩ is the prohibition ‘do not do’ (ኢ + jussive 2mp).

sentences.t: ወዘንተ ፡ ሰሚዖሙ ፡ ኀደጉ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ፍትወተ ፡ ሥጋ ፡ ወይቤልዎ ፡ ለእግዚእነ ፡ ናሁኬ ፡ ኀደግነ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ወተለውናከ ፡ ምንት ፡ ዐስብነ ።
sentences.l: And-this having-heard-they, they-left all desire-of flesh, and-said-to-him, to-our-Lord: behold-now we-left all and-followed-you; what is-our-reward?
sentences.i: And when they heard this they left every desire of the flesh, and said to our Lord: Behold, we have left everything and followed you; what is our reward?
sentences.n: ሰሚዖሙ is a converb ‘having heard they’ (ሰምዐ). ኀደጉ ‘they left’. ይቤልዎ ለእግዚእነ ‘they said to him, to our Lord’ (the pronoun ‘him’ is doubled by the ለ- noun). ናሁኬ ‘behold now’; ኀደግነ ‘we left’; ተለውናከ ‘we followed you’ (ተለወ + -ከ). ምንት ዐስብነ ‘what (is) our reward?’ The question is Peter's in Matthew 19:27 (‘we have left everything and followed you; what shall we have?’), where the Lord's answer includes sitting on twelve thrones, which unit 24 echoes.

sentences.t: ወይቤሎሙ ፡ መድኀኒነ ፡ እስመ ፡ ተመሰልክሙ ፡ በሥጋ ፡ ከመ ፡ መላእክት ፡ ወትገብሩ ፡ ኀይለ ፡ ከማየ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-said-to-them, our-Saviour: since you-were-made-like in-flesh as angels, and-you-do power like-me;
sentences.i: And our Saviour said to them: Since you have been made like angels in the flesh, and you do mighty works as I do;
sentences.n: መድኀኒነ ‘our Saviour’ (መድኀኒ + -ነ). ተመሰልክሙ ‘you (pl.) have been likened’, perfect of ተመሰለ, በሥጋ ‘in the flesh’, ከመ መላእክት ‘like angels’ (compare Matthew 22:30, where the risen are ‘like angels’). ወትገብሩ ኀይለ ‘and you do power’ ከማየ ‘like me’ (ከማ + -የ ‘me’). The clause is the first half of an argument: because you have mastered the flesh, the powers that follow are yours.

sentences.t: ወናሁ ፡ አባሕኩክ ፡ ሙ ፡ ታንሥኡ ፡ ምዉታነ ፡ ወወሀብኩክሙ ፡ ስልጣነ ፡ ትፈውሱ ፡ ድውያነ ፡ ወትኪዲ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ኀይለ ፡ ጸላኢ ፤
sentences.l: and-behold I-gave-you-leave(?) (that) you-raise the-dead, and-I-gave-you authority (that) you-heal the-sick and-(that) you-trample all power-of the-enemy;
sentences.i: and behold, I have given you leave (?) to raise the dead, and I have given you authority to heal the sick and to trample all the power of the enemy;
sentences.n: The source writes አባሕኩክ ፡ ሙ with a wordspace in the middle; it is one word, አባሕኩክሙ ‘I (have) … you (pl.)’. The verb is አባሐ (?), which I take as ‘permit, authorise’ (?). ታንሥኡ ምዉታነ ‘you raise the dead’ (አንሥአ, with ምዉታን ‘the dead’); ወወሀብኩክሙ ስልጣነ ‘and I gave you authority’; ትፈውሱ ድውያነ ‘you heal the sick’. ትኪዲ is from ከይደ ‘tread, trample’, written with the 2fs ending -ኢ (?) where the plural ትኪዱ is expected. The three powers follow Matthew 10:8 and Luke 10:19 (‘authority to tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy’). ጸላኢ ‘the enemy’, i.e. Satan.

sentences.t: ወበዳግም ፡ ምጽአትየ ፡ ትኴንንዎሙ ፡ ወታስተኀፍርዎሙ ፡ ለ፲ወ፪ ፡ ነገደ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዘኢአምኑ ፡ ኪያየ ፡ ወአስተሐቀሩ ፡ ስብሐትየ ፤
sentences.l: and-at-the-second my-coming you-will-judge-them and-you-will-shame-them, the-twelve tribes-of Israel, because they-did-not-believe in-me and-they-scorned my-glory;
sentences.i: and at my second coming you will judge them and put them to shame, the twelve tribes of Israel, because they did not believe in me and scorned my glory;
sentences.n: በዳግም ምጽአትየ ‘at the second coming of mine’ (ዳግም ‘second’, ምጽአት ‘coming’). ትኴንንዎሙ ‘you will judge/condemn them’ (imperfect 2mp + them) and ታስተኀፍርዎሙ ‘you will shame them’ (the causative አስተኀፈረ of ኀፈረ ‘be ashamed’). ለ፲ወ፪ ነገደ is ‘the twelve tribes’, spoken ዐሠርቱ ወክልኤቱ (ʿäśärtu wä-kəlʾetu), with ነገድ ‘tribe’. Compare Matthew 19:28 (‘you will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel’). በእንተ ዘኢአምኑ ኪያየ ‘because of what they did not believe, me’ (ኪያየ ‘me’ is the accusative pronoun). አስተሐቀሩ ‘they despised’; ስብሐትየ ‘my glory, praise’.

sentences.t: ወለእለሰ ፡ የአምኑ ፡ ብየ ፡ ታዐብይዎሙ ፡ ወታስተፌሥሕዎሙ ፡ ምስሌክሙ ፡ በመንግሥትየ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-those-but who believe in-me, you-will-magnify-them and-you-will-make-them-rejoice with-you in-my-kingdom.
sentences.i: But as for those who do believe in me, you will exalt them and make them rejoice with you in my kingdom.
sentences.n: ወለእለሰ ‘and as for those who’; የአምኑ ብየ ‘they believe in me’ (ብየ ‘in me’). ታዐብይዎሙ ‘you will make them great, exalt them’ (አዐበየ) and ታስተፌሥሕዎሙ ‘you will make them rejoice’ (አስተፈሥሐ); ምስሌክሙ ‘with you’; በመንግሥትየ ‘in my kingdom’. The saying turns the disciples' reward into a share for believers. The row of ፨ ends the chapter.

sentences.t: ፸፭ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ባቢሎን ።
sentences.l: 75. Concerning king-of Babylon.
sentences.i: Chapter 75: Concerning the king of Babylon.
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ባቢሎን is Babylon. The number ፸፭ is 75, spoken ሰብዓ ወኀምስቱ (säbʿa wä-ḫäməstu).

sentences.t: ወንጉሠ ፡ ባቢሎንሂ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ሴም ፡ ውእቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-king-of Babylon-also, seed-of Shem is-he;
sentences.i: And the king of Babylon too is of the seed of Shem;
sentences.n: ወንጉሠ ባቢሎንሂ ‘and king-of Babylon-also’, with the same enclitic -ሂ as in unit 12 (ch. 74). The statement repeats the form of unit 12.

sentences.t: ወንነግረክሙ ፡ ጥዩቀ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ሴም ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ባቢሎን ።
sentences.l: and-we-tell-you accurately that seed-of Shem (is) king-of Babylon.
sentences.i: and we tell you for certain that the king of Babylon is of the seed of Shem.
sentences.n: ንነግረክሙ ‘we tell you’ (imperfect 1cp of ነገረ + -ክሙ); ጥዩቀ ‘accurately, for certain’, an adjective in the accusative used as an adverb. ከመ ‘that’ introduces the content: ዘርአ ሴም ንጉሠ ባቢሎን ‘(it is) seed-of Shem, king-of Babylon’. The narrator stresses the point, as with the Midianite king above.

sentences.t: ወሀሎ ፡ በውእቱ ፡ መዋዕል ፡ በመንግሥተ ፡ ምናሴ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ወሀሎ ፡ ፩ ፡ ብእሲ ፡ ዘስሙ ፡ ከርሚን ፡ ፈራሄ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወይገብር ፡ ብዙኀ ፡ ምጽዋተ ፡ ለነዳያነ ፡ እስራኤል ፤
sentences.l: And-there-was in-that days in-the-reign-of Manasseh king-of Israel, and-there-was one man whose-name Karmin, fearer-of God, and-he-does much almsgiving for-the-poor-of Israel;
sentences.i: And in those days, in the reign of Manasseh, king of Israel, there was a man whose name was Karmin, a God-fearing man, and he did much almsgiving for the poor of Israel;
sentences.n: ወሀሎ ‘and there was’; በውእቱ መዋዕል ‘in those days’; በመንግሥተ ምናሴ ‘in the kingdom-of Manasseh’ (the Bible has Manasseh as king of Judah, 2 Kings 21; here ‘king of Israel’). ፩ is ‘one’, spoken አሐዱ (ʾäḥädu); ብእሲ ‘a man’. ዘስሙ ከርሚን ‘whose name (is) Karmin’; I do not identify the name (?). ፈራሄ እግዚኣብሔር ‘fearer-of God’ (the construct of ፈራሂ). ወይገብር ብዙኀ ምጽዋተ ‘and he does much almsgiving’ (ምጽዋት ‘alms’), ለነዳያነ እስራኤል ‘for the poor of Israel’.

sentences.t: ወሶበሂ ፡ ይሠውዕ ፡ ለቤተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ይገብር ፡ በንጹሕ ፡ ወዓሥራተሂ ፡ ይሁብ ፡ አመክዒቦ ፡ ወበኵሉ ፡ ፍኖቱ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ወኢምንተኒ ፡ እኩየ ፡ በቅድሜሁ ፤
sentences.l: and-whenever he-offers-sacrifice to-the-house-of God he-does in-purity, and-tithes-also he-gives in-full-measure(?), and-in-all his-way good, and-there-is-not and-nothing evil before-him;
sentences.i: and whenever he offered sacrifice at the house of God he did it in purity, and he gave his tithes too, in full measure (?); and in all his way he was good, and there was nothing evil in his sight;
sentences.n: ወሶበሂ ‘and whenever’; ይሠውዕ ‘he sacrifices’; ለቤተ እግዚኣብሔር ‘to the house of God’; ይገብር በንጹሕ ‘he does (it) in purity’. ዓሥራተሂ ይሁብ ‘tithes (ዓሥራት, ‘tenths’) too he gives’ (compare Deuteronomy 14:22 and Malachi 3:10). አመክዒቦ is a word I cannot place (?); I read ‘in full measure’ from ምክዕብ ‘cube, a measure’ as a guess. በኵሉ ፍኖቱ ሠናይ ‘in all his way (he was) good’. ወአልቦ ወኢምንተኒ እኩየ በቅድሜሁ ‘and there was not anything evil before him’, a double negative in Geʿez for emphasis; the portrait of an upright man is close to Job 1:1.

sentences.t: ወሰይጣንሰ ፡ ጸላኤ ፡ ሠናያት ፡ ይቀንእ ፡ ላዕሌሁ ፡ በዘ ፡ ርእየ ፡ ሠናየ ፡ ፍኖቶ ።
sentences.l: And-Satan-but, enemy-of good-things, is-envious against-him, because he-saw good his-way.
sentences.i: But Satan, the enemy of good things, was envious of him, because he saw that his way was good.
sentences.n: ሰይጣንሰ ‘Satan, for his part’; ጸላኤ ሠናያት ‘enemy-of good-things’ (ጸላኢ in the construct). ይቀንእ ላዕሌሁ ‘he envies against him’ (ቀንአ ‘be zealous, envious’). በዘ ርእየ ‘because he saw’; ሠናየ ፍኖቶ ‘his way (as) good’. As in the Book of Job, Satan watches a righteous man; here he acts out of envy.

sentences.t: ወውእቱሰ ፡ ብእሲ ፡ ባዕል ፡ ጥቀ ፡ አግማለ ፡ ወአፍራሰ ፡ ወመራዕየ ፡ እንስሳ ፡ ወአልህምተ ፡ ወርቀ ፡ ወብሩረ ፡ ወአልባሰ ፡ ክቡረ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-but a-man rich very, of-camels and-horses and-herds-of livestock and-oxen, gold and-silver and-clothing precious;
sentences.i: And he was a very rich man, with camels and horses, herds of livestock and oxen, gold and silver, and precious clothing;
sentences.n: ወውእቱሰ ‘and he, for his part’; ባዕል ጥቀ ‘rich indeed’ (ጥቀ ‘very’). The nouns are in the accusative as a list of what he owned: አግማል ‘camels’, አፍራስ ‘horses’, መራዕየ እንስሳ ‘herds-of livestock’, አልህምት ‘oxen’, ወርቅ ‘gold’, ብሩር ‘silver’, አልባስ ክቡር ‘precious clothing’ (ክቡር ‘precious, honoured’). The list is also close to Job 1:3 (camels, oxen, asses).

sentences.t: ወይሴሲ ፡ በቅለ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ በአርማቴም ፡ ሀገረ ፡ እስራኤል ።
sentences.l: and-he-tends(?) the-king's grass in-Armathaim city-of Israel.
sentences.i: and he looked after (?) the king's herbage (?) in Armathaim, a city of Israel.
sentences.n: ይሴሲ is the verb ሴሰየ ‘supply with food, feed’ (?), so ‘he tended/supplied’ (?). በቅለ ንጉሥ ‘the king's herbage, greens’ (በቅል), though elsewhere in this text በቅል is ‘mule’, and ‘the king's mules’ would suit ‘feed’ equally well (?). አርማቴም is Armathaim, the Ramathaim of 1 Samuel 1:1 and the Arimathea of Matthew 27:57; the text calls it a city of Israel. The sentence gives Karmin a job in the royal household's service.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ደወሉሰ ፡ ብሔረ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ክፍለ ፡ አበዊሁ ፤
sentences.l: For his-home-region(?)-but was the-land-of Judah, portion-of his-fathers;
sentences.i: For his home district (?) was the land of Judah, the portion of his fathers;
sentences.n: ደወሉሰ ‘his ደወል, for its part’: ደወል is ‘bell’ in the lexicon, so here ‘home district’ is only a guess from the sense (?). ብሔረ ይሁዳ ‘land-of Judah’, ክፍለ አበዊሁ ‘portion-of his fathers’ (አበው plural of አብ ‘father’ + -ሁ). That is, Karmin was a man of Judah's tribe who moved away.

sentences.t: ወበእንተ ፡ ፍቅረ ፡ ንዋይ ፡ ሖረ ፡ ውስተ ፡ አርማቴም ፡ ከመ ፡ ይንበር ፡ ወአንበርዎ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ በእንተ ፡ ብዕሉ ፡ እስመ ፡ ቦ ፡ ብዙኀ ፡ ንዋየ ፡ ወይፈርህ ፡ መኳንንተ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: and-because-of love-of wealth he-went to-Armathaim to-dwell, and-they-settled-him, Israel, because-of his-wealth, for there-is-to-him much property, and-he-fears the-princes.
sentences.i: and for love of wealth he went to Armathaim to settle, and Israel settled him there because of his wealth, for he had much property, and he feared the princes.
sentences.n: በእንተ ፍቅረ ንዋይ ‘because of love-of wealth’ (ንዋይ ‘goods, vessels’). ሖረ ‘went’; ከመ ይንበር ‘in order that he might dwell’ (subjunctive); ወአንበርዎ ‘and they made him settle’ (causative አንበረ + him) with እስራኤል ‘Israel’ as subject. ቦ ብዙኀ ንዋየ ‘there is to him much property’ (ቦ ‘he has’). ወይፈርህ መኳንንተ ‘and he fears princes’ (መኳንንት ‘rulers’), probably explaining why he wanted to settle among Israel in the royal city. The part ends here, with the story of Karmin still unfolding.
